territorial_scope.description: Applies to ICTS transactions involving the United States and to United States persons wherever located, and reaches foreign persons' ICTS transactions that would be prohibited if performed in the United States.

evidence.quote: Any approval, financing, facilitation, or guarantee by a United States person, wherever located, of an ICTS Transaction by a foreign person

summary.short: Amends 15 CFR Part 791 to set procedures for the Secretary of Commerce to review and prohibit or mitigate ICTS transactions involving foreign adversary-linked persons, for parties to such transactions. Binding prohibitions, recordkeeping duties and civil and criminal penalties apply.
summary.long: Federal Register rule amending 15 CFR Part 791 under E.O. 13873 and IEEPA, governing Commerce review of information and communications technology and services (ICTS) transactions involving persons owned by, controlled by, or subject to the jurisdiction of foreign adversaries. Revises definitions (including Covered ICTS Transaction, Dealing in, Importation and foreign-adversary persons), the scope in § 791.3 (ICTS integral to listed categories including connected software applications, data hosting and critical and emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence), and review criteria in § 791.103. Procedure: interagency notification with 21 days to comment (§ 791.104); Initial Determination (§ 791.105); response within 30 days (§ 791.107); interagency consultation (§ 791.108); Final Determination within 180 days of service (§ 791.109), classifying a transaction as prohibited, not prohibited or permitted with mitigation. Notified persons must retain records for at least ten years (§ 791.106). Prohibited transactions and related conduct are set out in § 791.200(a). Civil penalties follow IEEPA (greater of $250,000 per violation, inflation-adjusted, or twice the transaction amount); criminal fines up to $1,000,000 and imprisonment up to 20 years apply on conviction.

notes: Annotated from the amendatory rule text as published in the Federal Register (Doc. 2024-28335, filed 12-5-24). No consolidated CFR text was used. Internal inconsistency: Amendment 7 removes the 'second parenthetical (d)' from § 791.4(d), but the § 791.4(d) text shown contains no such parenthetical. The text uses 'Secretary' and 'Department' interchangeably in §§ 791.100, 791.107 and 791.200. The stray space in 'Federal Register .' (§ 791.105(d), § 791.109(f)) is typographical. Foreign adversary countries and persons named in § 791.4 are not coded as entities. any acquisition, importation, transfer, installation, dealing in, or use of any information and communications technology or service, including but not limited to connected software applications, (ICTS Transaction)
Covered ICTS Transaction means an ICTS Transaction or a class of ICTS Transactions that meets the criteria set forth in § 791.3.
Dealing in means the activity of buying, selling, reselling, receiving, licensing, or acquiring ICTS, or otherwise doing or engaging in business involving the conveyance of ICTS.
Importation means the process or activity of bringing foreign ICTS to or into the United States, regardless of the means of conveyance, including via electronic transmission.

United States person means any United States citizen; any permanent resident alien; any entity organized under the laws of the United States or any jurisdiction within the United States (including such entity's foreign branches); or any person in the United States.

obligations.summary: The Secretary periodically reviews the list of foreign adversaries in consultation with appropriate agency heads and may amend it. The Secretary's determination is based on multiple sources listed in paragraph (c).

evidence.quote: The Secretary will periodically review this list in consultation with appropriate agency heads

obligations.summary: In reviewing ICTS Transactions, the Secretary considers relevant information held by or available to the Federal Government, and determines in consultation with agency heads whether an ICTS Transaction involves foreign adversary-linked ICTS and whether a Covered ICTS Transaction poses an undue or unacceptable risk.

evidence.quote: Consider any and all relevant information held by, or otherwise made available to, the Federal Government

obligations.summary: A person required by the Secretary must furnish complete information, under oath, in reports or otherwise, including documents and records as the Secretary requires, relating to any act, transaction or property.
obligations.conditional_on: when the Secretary requires information from the person

evidence.quote: the Secretary may require any person to furnish under oath, in the form of reports or otherwise

obligations.summary: During a review the Secretary assesses whether the transaction is a Covered ICTS Transaction, involves ICTS linked to a foreign adversary, and poses an undue or unacceptable risk, and then either ends review or proceeds under the following sections.
obligations.conditional_on: when a review of an ICTS Transaction is under way

evidence.quote: As part of the review, the Secretary will assess whether the transaction

obligations.summary: The Secretary memorialises the assessment, provides it to the appropriate agency heads, and gives them twenty-one days to comment in writing. The Secretary may presume an agency has no comments if none are received within that period.
obligations.conditional_on: If the Secretary assesses that an ICTS Transaction meets the criteria under § 791.103(b)

evidence.quote: the Secretary shall memorialize that assessment, provide the assessment to the appropriate agency heads, and offer the appropriate agency heads twenty-one (21) days to comment in writing

obligations.summary: Where the Covered ICTS Transaction meets the criteria, the Secretary issues a dated and signed written Initial Determination stating the reasons, whether a prohibition or mitigation is proposed, and the factual basis. The Secretary gives agency heads at least twenty-one calendar days' notice and serves the Initial Determination on the parties, without classified information.
obligations.conditional_on: If the Secretary determines that the Covered ICTS Transaction meets the criteria set forth in § 791.103

evidence.quote: Make a written Initial Determination, which shall be dated and signed by the Secretary

obligations.summary: A notified person must retain records relating to the transaction for no less than ten years after a Final Determination, or as the Final Determination indicates. If no Initial Determination is made within ten years of notice of review, retention runs ten years from the initial notification.
obligations.conditional_on: Upon notification that an ICTS Transaction is under review

evidence.quote: a notified person must immediately take steps to retain any and all records relating to such Transaction

obligations.summary: Submissions by a party in response to an Initial Determination must be in writing, may not exceed fifty pages without prior approval, and must clearly mark any business confidential information. The party's response is due within thirty days of service of the Initial Determination.
obligations.conditional_on: When a party to a transaction responds to an Initial Determination under § 791.107

evidence.quote: All submissions under this section must be made in writing.

obligations.summary: The Secretary considers any party submission, gives written notice of the proposed Final Determination, and consults and seeks concurrence from all appropriate agency heads before issuing it. An agency objection must be submitted by its Deputy Secretary or equivalent within fourteen days.
obligations.conditional_on: Upon receipt of a party submission under § 791.107

evidence.quote: the Secretary shall provide notice in writing of the proposed Final Determination and consult with and seek concurrence from all appropriate agency heads

obligations.summary: For each Covered ICTS Transaction with an Initial Determination, the Secretary issues a written, signed and dated Final Determination (prohibited, not prohibited, or permitted with mitigation) within 180 days of serving the Initial Determination unless extended in writing. The Secretary directs necessary means where prohibited, sends the determination to parties and agency heads, and publishes notices in the Federal Register.
obligations.conditional_on: Unless the Secretary, at the Secretary's sole discretion, determines in writing that additional time is necessary

evidence.quote: the Secretary shall issue the Final Determination within 180 days of serving the Initial Determination

obligations.summary: No person may be a party to an ICTS Transaction prohibited by a Final Determination, aid or engage in conduct known to be prohibited, or be party to a transaction contrary to mitigation terms. Transactions made to evade prohibitions, conspiracies, US-person approval or financing of prohibited foreign transactions, and false or misleading statements to the Department are also prohibited.

evidence.quote: No person shall be a party to an ICTS Transaction that is prohibited by a Final Determination issued under this part, unless authorized by the Secretary.

obligations.summary: A person who has made a representation, statement or certification to the Department about an ICTS Transaction review must notify the Department in writing of any change of material fact or intention, immediately upon receiving information that would lead a reasonably prudent person to know of such a change. Earlier representations remain continuing until such notice.
obligations.conditional_on: Upon receipt of information indicating a change of material fact or intention from a previous representation to the Department

evidence.quote: shall notify the Department, in writing, of any change of any material fact or intention from that previously represented
